name: scan_content
description: Scan untrusted text for prompt-injection signals. Static and rule-based: the text is never executed and nothing is fetched or written. `source_type` selects the policy - `unknown` (the default) behaves like `source` and is the honest reverse-deployment number; pass `fixture` or `documentation` when you know. `path_hint` only derives the type while `source_type` is `unknown`. Findings carry no raw text unless `include_snippet` is true; a returned snippet has credential-shaped substrings replaced by `<redacted:class>` markers, best effort and never a secret-free guarantee. `include_raw_snippet` adds the unredacted copy alongside. `emit_bundle` (default false) adds an `evidence_bundle` object holding the exact returned payload plus digests of that payload and of the scan input, so `verify_evidence` can re-derive it later; the digest is not a signature and proves neither correctness nor that a scan ran. `truncated` is only reported when `max_findings` is below 32; at 32 the scanner's own per-file cap applies and the flag is always false. Cancellation cannot be observed before the call returns. AuraScan's injection detector is a static, rule-based first signal — it reports text that looks like instructions aimed at an AI reader, nothing is executed, and the confidence value is a policy label, not a precision estimate.

name: scan_path
description: Scan one bounded UTF-8 file from disk. The path derives `source_type` and must resolve inside a configured root. Read-only: the file is read once, nothing is written. Symlinks are followed only while they stay inside a root; non-regular files are refused. Findings carry no raw text unless `include_snippet` is true; a returned snippet has credential-shaped substrings replaced by `<redacted:class>` markers, best effort and never a secret-free guarantee. `include_raw_snippet` adds the unredacted copy alongside. `emit_bundle` (default false) adds an `evidence_bundle` object holding the exact returned payload plus digests of that payload and of the decoded scan input, so `verify_evidence` can re-derive it later; the digest is not a signature and proves neither correctness nor that a scan ran, and it covers decoded text rather than raw bytes. `truncated` follows the same rule as `scan_content`. AuraScan's injection detector is a static, rule-based first signal — it reports text that looks like instructions aimed at an AI reader, nothing is executed, and the confidence value is a policy label, not a precision estimate.

name: audit_agent_config
description: Audit one agent/MCP configuration document as untrusted data. Static: no file is opened, no command is run, no permission is evaluated. Reports broad tool grants, dangerous hook correlations, command behaviour correlations and JSON shape problems, with line numbers. It establishes static configuration only - not that a server starts, a grant is effective, or a command executes. `mcp-manifest` checks JSON shape and grants only and does not correlate commands; `cursor-mcp-manifest` (the default) adds command-behaviour correlations and is the surface to use for any document with `mcpServers` command/args fields. Duplicate keys are rejected, not last-wins: a document with two `mcpServers` keys reports an invalid-shape finding and `coverage_complete: false`. AuraScan's injection detector is a static, rule-based first signal — it reports text that looks like instructions aimed at an AI reader, nothing is executed, and the confidence value is a policy label, not a precision estimate.

name: audit_agent_runtime
description: Report execution authority and readable project secret classes for one external agent surface under the server's first configured root. Static and read-only: the agent, a model, an MCP server, a hook and project code are never started or contacted. Codex, Claude Code and Cursor include their built-in shell authority; hook and MCP stdio commands add explicit channels. The projection is aggregate only: it returns no inspected file paths, root path, channel locations, secret paths or input digests. `coverage_complete: false` is not a clean result and the caller must not treat it as one. Secret classes are counted from fixed project-relative candidates; home, environment, keyring and socket credentials are explicitly not inspected. This is a blast-radius preflight, not a model-safety verdict, containment, or proof that a trigger exists. AuraScan's injection detector is a static, rule-based first signal — it reports text that looks like instructions aimed at an AI reader, nothing is executed, and the confidence value is a policy label, not a precision estimate.

name: security_audit
description: Check the local host against bounded AUR campaign intelligence, bundled vendor advisories and host indicators. Runs in offline mode by design: no network at all, and no state is written - the campaign feed comes from the packaged assets or a previously refreshed cache, and `arch-audit` is skipped. It runs one read-only process (`pacman -Q`, bounded to 30 s) and stats or reads the reported artifact paths under `/etc`, `/usr/lib`, `/usr/bin` and `/usr/local/bin` (including `/etc/ufw/user.rules` and `/etc/ufw/user6.rules`), `/root/pamkeys`, `/var/log/pacman.log{,.1}`, `/sys/fs/bpf` and the AUR helper cache. Findings are exposure evidence: a package-name match is not proof a malicious commit executed, and no match is not proof of integrity. AuraScan never removes or quarantines anything. The honesty line in `instructions` applies to the injection detector; this tool additionally runs one read-only process. `include_evidence` (default false) adds each finding's `evidence` array. That array is host-local: it carries absolute paths of matched artifacts, `hidden_*` BPF object names and Tailscale peer markers, so a result pasted into a chat discloses this host's layout. `arch_audit.findings[].evidence` is not returned at all - the arch audit does not run offline today, so its evidence is unreachable and must not be assumed.

name: verify_evidence
description: Checks that an AuraScan bundle is internally consistent and, when you supply the source, that it still re-derives. Three separable questions: the bundle's own digest is recomputed, the bundled payload is re-hashed against `payload_sha256`, and the same tool is re-run and its payload hashed against the bundled one. Supply at most one source - `path` (resolved inside a configured root, the same guards as `scan_path`; an unusable path is `unchecked`, not an error) or `content` - or neither, which leaves `consistency` at `unchecked` and `notes` at `source_absent`. `consistent` needs every internal check to agree, including the re-derivation; it never means the bundle is true. Read-only: two bounded file reads at most, nothing written. It does not verify: (1) `origin` - anyone can recompute the digest, there is no key and no signature, so it says nothing about who produced the bundle or when; (2) `truth` - reproduction proves the same rules still fire on the same bytes, not that the rules are right or complete; (3) `no_tamper` - an editor who changes a finding and recomputes `bundle_sha256` passes every check here; (4) `execution` - nothing is executed, a scan is static text analysis; (5) `file_identity_beyond_bytes` - only bytes are compared, so the same bytes at a different path are indistinguishable; (6) `rule_catalog` - only the version strings are compared, catalog contents are not hashed.

annotations.title: Check an evidence bundle against its own source

name: security_audit_online
description: Same bounded host audit as `security_audit`, plus one HTTPS GET of the packaged campaign manifest source and the `arch-audit --json` pass the offline tool skips. `refresh` defaults true; `refresh: false` suppresses only AuraScan's own fetch - `arch-audit` may still reach its own feed and is the only other egress, so `refresh: false` is not the same thing as no network. The refresh is validated (2 MiB cap, UTF-8, name syntax, digest) and held in memory: nothing is written by AuraScan, the offline cache under `$XDG_STATE_HOME/aurascan/security-intel` is read if present and never written, and `security_audit`'s own result is left untouched. Only that cache's own contents are trusted exactly as much as the offline tool trusts it. 3xx responses are rejected *before* the redirect target is contacted, so there is no silent cross-host beacon, and proxy environment variables are not inherited (`no_proxy`-style escapes and a mandatory corporate proxy are both unsupported here). `verified: shape-only` - size, UTF-8, name syntax and digest, computed by this same process and not signed - is the whole claim, so DNS rebinding and a TLS-terminating MITM remain. It runs one filtered-environment `pacman -Q` (bounded to 30 s) and, unless `include_arch_audit` is false, one `arch-audit` (45 s); the children get only an allowlisted environment, though their own captured stderr still reaches `notes` and `arch_audit.error` unfiltered, and `which("arch-audit")` resolves on the server's `PATH` rather than the filtered one. A failed refresh is not an error: `isError` stays false, `status` drops to `partial` on an otherwise clean run, and the caller branches on `status` plus `refresh.status`/`refresh.error` (`redirect_rejected`, `http_error`, `network_error`, `invalid_feed`, `campaign_unavailable`, `unknown`) while validated bundled or cached data is retained. `include_evidence` (default false) carries the same host-local evidence disclosure as `security_audit`, and here `arch_audit.findings[].evidence` really is reachable, so it follows the flag too. Budget is 110 s under the client's 120; cancellation is advisory and only observed at phase boundaries, so the budget is the hard bound. The honesty line in `instructions` applies to the injection detector; this tool does not certify a package or a host either.
